#5119. The Best Winter Jackets for Men, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

We tried more than 40 options to find the ones worth wearing all season.

MEN’S HEALTH EDITORS spend a lot of time outdoors. We commute to our NYC office, then juggle the gym, errands, and weekend outings. So when cold weather hits, we need winter coats that can get us through nearly every icy scenario imaginable. Gone are the days when staying warm meant looking like a walking snowman. Today’s outerwear pairs advanced insulation with weather-resistant fabrics and thoughtful details to help keep you warm when the temperatures drop. The best designs layer comfortably, move well, and still look sharp.

As someone who tests gear year-round—and as part of a team that’s been reviewing winter coats since 2019—I’ve worn everything from lightweight puffers on frosty commutes to parkas in sub-zero conditions. Along the way, the Men’s Health style team has put more than 40 coats through real-life use: daily city commutes, snowy trail days, and ski trips. We look at how warm they actually feel, how well they move, how tough the materials are, and whether they look good off the rack. And after all that, Mack Weldon, Columbia, and Canada Goose rose to the top as the best winter coats for men.

I’ve been getting my wear out of Mack Weldon’s WarmKnit Air Hooded Jacket for the past year and it surprised me with its performance. At first glance, you’d think it’s just a lightweight puffer built for those mild 50- to 60-degree temps. But I found it could hang in the 40s, too—and still keep me warm. That’s thanks to its Thinsulate fill, synthetic insulation made of ultra-fine fibers, which does the heavy lifting without making me feel like a bloated marshmallow. It’s water- and wind-resistant, so a little drizzle or gusty wind doesn’t ruin a commute either.

The snap-button front and the two-way zipper make it easy to get in and out of, and the structured hood actually stays put, protecting your head without flopping around or blowing off. Just like most of Mack Weldon’s winter collection, sporty casual meets performance is the vibe here, so you can wear it with anything from a sweatsuit to a casual crewneck over chinos. With bonded quilting and interior pockets, it's both functional and polished, so it works for weekend hikes or casual dinners.

That said, there are trade‑offs. The jacket’s waist‑length cut means it won’t cover your core the way a mid‑thigh parka does, so in truly cold winter conditions you’ll feel more exposed around hips and lower back. If you need serious warmth for winter storms, opt for a longer cut; if you want a versatile everyday coat for mild to moderately cold weather, this is a standout value pick.

For days when you want warmth without the bulk, this Columbia down jacket delivers in spades. It uses Omni‑Heat reflective lining—those tiny silver dots that bounce your body heat back at you—which helps keep heat where you want it even as temperatures dip and winds pick up. It’s the kind of jacket you reach for when you want to feel cozy without feeling weighed down.

The 650‑fill down has enough loft to stay warm without ballooning your silhouette, and the baffle construction keeps insulation evenly distributed while creating a streamlined look that’s more polished than many puffers of similar warmth. Columbia also packs in tech‑forward features like HeatSeal construction to trap warmth while still allowing breathability and Omni‑Shield for moisture resistance and stain repellency—handy when you’re trudging through slush or, as I once did, surviving a spilled coffee on the way to the bus.

What I appreciate most is how easily it layers: It slips over a fleece or hoodie without feeling stiff, and it’s comfortable enough to wear all day whether you’re heading to work or exploring snowy trails. It’s not the warmest jacket around, but for everyday winter conditions where you want mobility and comfort with insulation, it’s a fantastic pick.

This is, quite simply, one of the best budget winter jackets we’ve tested—and it’s worth your attention even if you usually steer clear of ultra‑affordable picks. Deals and Trends Editor Tim Kohut wore the coat zipped up, and found that the heavyweight insulation did a solid job at keeping the shivers at bay on a brisk walk to the train — all without overheating once he hit the warm subway platform.

The polyester shell is water-repellent, not waterproof, so he can survive light showers without them soaking through to his clothes. It may not be the best option for heavy rain, so if you’re staring down a prolonged rainstorm, an umbrella or rain layer is still a smart call. Its relaxed fit is roomy enough for you to fit a chunky sweater underneath without bulk. Kohut rocked a T-shirt and chunky cardigan, and did not feel like the Michelin Man after being fully zipped up. The hood doesn’t cinch tight — one of the few real drawbacks — which lets cold air sneak in on windier days, but it is fleece‑lined for extra comfort and warmth.

Pockets are straightforward but functional, and the simple styling means this jacket works for daily commuting as easily as casual weekends. For the price, it’s a total win if you want something warm, reliable, and unfussy without dropping big cash.

Our Grooming Editor Sean Zucker wore this parka in every cold-weather situation: long commutes, chilly hikes, snowball fights. It has a slim puffer design but with a longer cut and more down, making it warmer for bone-chilling morning walks to the coffee shop. Zucker recently got caught in a sudden downpour, and the waterproof—not just water-resistant—shell kept him completely dry. On a freezing 30-degree cold and windy day, he stayed warm and comfortable the entire time. Plus, the storm cuffs blocked icy gusts from sneaking in at the sleeves.

He also appreciated the two-way zipper, which you don’t see on a lot of winter coats. It made hopping on and off the subway or sitting at a café easy without feeling restricted. While the insulated hood isn’t super spacious, it cinches close enough to trap heat. The fit is stylish without feeling bulky, and his hands fit perfectly in the pockets—small detail, but it really makes a difference when it’s freezing out. Yes, it’s an investment piece, but with premium 700-fill down warmth, waterproof and windproof protection, and thoughtful features, this parka is a true workhorse built to handle harsh conditions.

Canada Goose’s coat may come with some sticker shock, but our Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan has made good use of it for the past three winters. He wears it to walk his two corgis, and between the snow, wind, and icy sidewalks, it keeps him warm without feeling like he’s lugging around a heavy sleeping bag. The Arctic Tech fabric—a polyester-cotton blend—has structure without stiffness, so it handles those brutal days when the wind tries to cut straight through you. Its longer silhouette offers extra coverage in snowy conditions. Not to mention, it’s a stylish coat, so you’re getting warmth and thoughtful design versus a bulky, shapeless puffer.

Like Fjallraven’s parka, this one has more pockets than your average coat—four outside, three inside. Two are great for thawing frozen mitts, and the others have flaps that help secure smaller essentials like a wallet, beanie, or winter gloves. There’s even a down-filled hood that feels toasty without making you feel stuffy, plus backpack-style straps if you want to carry it hands-free while running errands or grabbing coffee.

Sure, it’s very pricey, but we had to bite the bullet and think about the bigger picture. Stepping outside doesn’t feel like wrestling with the elements anymore. Between warmth, thoughtful design, and sleek style, it’s become our go-to armor for extreme weather—and it’s already survived three ruthless winter seasons in a row.

Men’s Health designer Jason Speakman took this burly parka from Fjallraven out on the slopes during a trip to Aspen. At 6 feet tall with a slender build, he found that this jacket wasn’t suffocating or too heavy, letting him flex, bend, and twist easily while carving turns or easing down steep trails. The fleece-lined hood with detachable faux fur edging kept his head and ears warm on icy chairlift rides, and he could easily remove the fur for a sleeker après-ski look. Thanks to the drawcords at the neck, it pulls tight around your face to shut out breezes.

This coat has eight pockets—more than any on the list—including roomy zippered chest pockets that fit slim essentials like a phone or cardholder. Its weight-to-warmth ratio is excellent; after five hours on the snow, Speakman stayed warm without feeling like he was wearing a stiff, overstuffed parka. The fit is generous, allowing space to pile base layers and still keep a clean profile.

Down and synthetic insulation are two of the most common options.

Synthetic insulation is made from polyester fibers, more affordable than down, and handles wet weather better. Popular options include PrimaLoft and Thinsulate, which use a blend of synthetic fibers designed to trap heat while remaining lightweight and breathable.

Down is made from clusters of goose or duck plumage, and is prized for its lightweight warmth. It compresses easily for packing and offers superior heat retention in dry conditions. Some coats even blend down and synthetic fill to combine the benefits of both.

Look for a waterproof shell, sealed seams, and a protective hood to help keep rain and snow from soaking through. Features like adjustable cuffs and storm flaps can also help block out wind and moisture. If you’re dealing with wet, snowy winters, prioritize a fully waterproof design over a water-resistant finish.

A winter coat should leave enough room to layer a sweater or hoodie without feeling bulky or restricting movement. The shoulders should sit comfortably, the sleeves should cover the wrists, and the hem should provide enough coverage for your needs. If you plan to wear it over heavier layers, consider sizing up, but always check the brand’s fit recommendations.

Look for fleece-lined hand pockets to keep your fingers warm and interior pockets to protect your phone, wallet, or AirPods from the cold. Extra details like zippered or hidden pockets add practicality, especially for commuting, travel, or outdoor adventures.

Our fashion team, led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, tested more than 40 winter coats in real-world conditions, from freezing city commutes to snowy hikes, ski trips, and travel days spent shuffling between cold-weather airports. If a coat claimed to handle winter, we made sure it proved it. We focused on warmth, durability, fit, mobility, and practicality. We paid attention to how each coat insulated in different temperatures, whether the materials could stand up to wind and wet weather, how well the coat moved with us during long days out, and whether the design felt useful rather than overbuilt.

Details like pocket placement, zippers, adjustability, and overall comfort played a big role too. After months of wear and side-by-side comparisons, only the top performers made our final list. These are the winter coats that stayed warm, held up, and made our lives easier—not just in theory, but in brutal winter reality.

For most of us, the terms "jacket" and "coat" are probably interchangeable. However, the main difference comes down to length and coverage. A winter coat's main objective is to keep you warm, which is why it's bigger and thicker, extends past the hips or toward the knees, and is filled with some type of insulation. A jacket, on the other hand, is considered a combination of style and warmth. Jackets don't typically go past the waist and they're designed to be worn indoors at times. Winter jackets can be layered more with outfits too—sometimes even under a coat.

Winter jackets can work as your main outer layer in cold weather, especially when they’re insulated and long enough to provide adequate coverage. For colder temperatures or extended time outdoors, a longer, more heavily insulated coat or parka can provide additional warmth and protection. The right choice ultimately depends on the weather, your activity level, and how much you plan to layer underneath.

Mutsamudu, Comoros, November 19, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, has released its November 2026 Proof of Reserves (PoR) report, independently audited by Hacken. The report shows MEXC’s solid reserve position, with user assets in every major asset backed by reserves above 1:1, demonstrating MEXC’s ongoing commitment to safeguarding user assets.

Spanning Proof of Liabilities, Proof of Ownership, Reserves Calculation, and Merkle Tree verification, Hacken’s November 2026 audit confirms substantial over-collateralisation across core holdings, standing at 318% for BTC, 122% for USDT, 112% for ETH, and 110% for USDC. Guided by its user-first philosophy, MEXC continues to enhance transparency to protect user assets and build trust. Since introducing Proof of Reserves in February 2023, MEXC has kept its wallet addresses and reserve data public, and its Merkle Tree system lets users verify at any time that their balances are included, without exposing other users’ data.   Reserves provide an extra layer of user protection. MEXC also manages user assets across cold and hot wallets under multi-signature authorization and layered risk controls, and maintains two dedicated funds. #5117. Just 18 Billion SHIB: Shiba Inu Netflow Signals Market Ease

The Shiba Inu exchange activity has remained bearish as the broader crypto market continues to face persistent selling pressure, causing major assets to retest multi-year lows.

While other leading cryptocurrencies are still facing intense sell-offs from traders, the Shiba Inu ecosystem is beginning to signal a shift in market trend.

Although momentum still remains down and Shiba Inu exchange activity has stayed bearish, the latest data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant shows that the intense selling pressure seen in the past day is finally easing.

The data shows that the Shiba Inu exchange netflow has faded to just about 18 billion SHIB on November 21, a substantial decrease from the nearly half a trillion SHIB recorded the previous day.

It is important to note that the current SHIB netflow still reflects a positive balance, which indicates sustained dominance by bear traders.

However, the slowdown to about 18 billion SHIB shows that SHIB selling has decreased significantly even though sellers are not yet fully wiped out, providing a relief signal amid the growing market fear.

Although the current positive balance in the SHIB netflow shows that the number of SHIB tokens moved to exchanges for sell-off attempts is about 18 billion higher than the number purchased, its price movement is already turning bullish.

Latest market data shows that Shiba Inu has surged by 1.51% over the last 24 hours, bringing its price to $0.000003625 as of the time of writing.

This suggests that demand is gradually returning to the SHIB ecosystem after multiple weeks of prolonged volatility. However, it remains uncertain whether the sudden price reversal is just a brief relief rally or a major recovery.

The early hours of the 20th of November saw Bitcoin [BTC] trading at $61,678 after a staggering 9.7% drop in the last 24 hours. Ethereum [ETH], following the crypto bloodbath, traded at $1,732 after experiencing a 3.7% slide in this time frame.

The crypto market’s current downfall is primarily due to persistent Spot ETF outflows and lingering fallout from last month’s Binance breach, which are making investors wary.

As the global cryptocurrency market cap fell 2.2% to $2.21 trillion in the last 24 hours at press time, the Crypto Fear & Greed Index slid to 12, indicating “extreme fear.”

After $306.5 million left Spot Bitcoin ETFs on the 18th of November, CoinGlass data showed that $582.3 million in outflows on the following day,  pushing this month’s outflows well past the $2.9 billion mark. Continued ETF bleeding signals that buyers continue to exit, leaving the market quite vulnerable to macro volatility.

Similarly, minutes from the October FOMC meeting, released on the 18th of November, showed that nearly all officials expect further rate hikes. Notably, Governor Christopher Waller even floated a half-point move for December.

With the Fed target at 3.75%–4.00%, digital assets will not have an easy battle.

Ever since investors have moved away from crypto and into AI, the former’s fall has been nearly constant. For the uninitiated, on the 18th of November, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, thus valuing the AI company at roughly $1.5 trillion.

The news drew massive investor attention, pulling capital away from crypto markets as a result.

Regardless, the long-term sentiment of crypto investors has already been sullied due to the October 29 Binance hack that resulted in $6.3 billion in stolen funds.

The crypto bloodbath will likely continue unless ETF flows stabilize or the Fed signals a pause. With the December 9 FOMC meeting as the only upcoming checkpoint, 60,000 is the next level for traders to watch. Losing it can tip Bitcoin deeper into the mid-50,000s.

#5115. XRP & XLM Hit Closest To ‘Value Area’ Among Major-Caps

Home » Altcoins » XRP & XLM Hit Closest To ‘Value Area’ Among Major-Caps

These two major-cap altcoin peers are hitting close to historically-undervalued territory: a highly-awaited bottom sign?

French analyst EGRAG compared the 4-hour charts of XRP, Ethereum, Hedera, Bitcoin, Solana, and Stellar to assess which assets are showing relative strength after recent lows.

The mainstream French crypto chart analyst’s review centers on price reaction, volume-profile location, and the distance remaining to each coin’s Value Area Low (VAL).

XRP is holding above its recent low without returning for a full retest. Solana is behaving in a similar fashion, maintaining its recovery structure. Stellar (XLM) is tracking XRP but appears slightly weaker. Ethereum (ETH) is retesting its lows, with a potential higher low developing.

Bitcoin (BTC) also retested and printed a slightly higher high. Hedera’s HBAR was retested with a lower high, the most shaky local structure among the six.

Distance to reclaim the VAL currently ranks as follows:

XRP and Stellar (XLM) are the nearest to re-entering their value areas. Bitcoin shows the more constructive local recovery structure among the larger-cap assets, even though it remains farther from its VAL than the two payment-focused names.

A double bottom is not confirmed simply because price holds above a prior low. The analysis treats bottoming as a process rather than a single candle. Early strength is marked by reclaiming the VAL.

#CRYPTO – 6 COINS, WHO IS SHOWING STRENGTH? #XRP – #ETH – #HBAR – #BTC – #SOL – #XLM FOLLOW THE PRICE, VOLUME & STRUCTURE! 👀The 4H charts reveal different reactions after the recent lows:▫️ #XRP: Holding above its recent low without a full retest.▫️ #ETH: Retesting the… pic.twitter.com/IFPBMuh7NJ

Structural confirmation requires a break of the local high. Stronger bullish conviction needs a reclaim of the Point of Control (POC) accompanied by volume.

The 4-hour volume profiles show each asset still trading below or near the lower boundary of its recent value area. Acceptance back inside the value area, followed by a move toward the POC, would shift the local bias.

Until that occurs, the charts remain in a recovery attempt rather than a confirmed reversal.

As of November 19, 2026, approximate prices stood near 63,700–64,000 for Bitcoin, $1,810 for Ethereum, $0.99 for XRP, $75 for Solana (SOL), $0.138 for Stellar (XLM) & $0.056 for Hedera Hashgraph (HBAR).

The broader market remains under moderate pressure, with Bitcoin dominance elevated and the Fear & Greed Index in Extreme Fear territory for consecutive days now.

The XRP coin & Stellar Lumens (XLM) are the nearest to early strength signals. Bitcoin’s slightly higher high on the retest is the more constructive structural note among the majors.

Confirmation across the group still requires a break of local highs and a return into the value area with volume. Until those conditions are met, the recovery remains unconfirmed.

#5114. The Best Sunglasses for Men, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Our fashion team recommends sunnies from Ray-Ban and Warby Parker.

A GREAT PAIR of sunglasses is the easiest way to upgrade your look. The right style can sharpen angular faces, soften sharper ones, or dress up even the most basic outfit—think square frames adding structure to a round face, or classic aviators elevating a T-shirt and jeans. They also protect your eyes from UV rays and cut down on glare, so you’re covered in both style and function. When picking your next pair, think about face shape and classic silhouettes.

Since 2020, our Men’s Health fashion team has tested over 50 styles—including aviators, wayfarers, and rounded frames—which all have stood the test of time due to their durability, versatility, and style. And don’t forget about occasions—what you wear to the beach, on a hike, or just around the city should match both your lifestyle and how you want to show up.

As a style editor for the past four years, I’ve tested over 25 different pairs of sunnies, but the Ray-Ban Wayfarer is still the best in its class. The signature silhouette—a slightly angular trapezoidal shape with thicker acetate frames—adds structure without looking too sharp, so it looks great on just about all round, oval, and even square faces and plays well with just about every fit.

First introduced in the ’50s as a casual alternative to metal frames, it was later worn by Tom Cruise, Michael Jackson, and George Michael, cementing its style icon status by the ’80s. In the past few years, Ray-Ban has updated it with a few stylish design tweaks—including a slightly smaller frame and more rounded lens shapes. We found it’s even easier to wear day-to-day to the office, lunch, or an early happy hour.

A wide range of frame and lens colors are available in the Original Wayfarer, but you can’t ever go wrong with the old-school black. We love this style because it looks great with every kind of vibe: a tailored suit, a tee and jeans, or just swim trunks on vacation. I found the acetate frame to be extra robust and heavy-duty at withstanding impact, courtesy of the seven-barrel hinges on each side. While this design does make the whole thing a bit heavier than most sunnies on this list, I never feel like it’s a burden on my face. I’ve found them comfortable whether I’m wearing them for a couple hours or from sunup to sundown.

Read More: Best Sunglasses Brands for Men

The Downing from Warby Parker is a safe bet because it will never go out of style. The slightly rounded shape traces back to midcentury optical styles that leaned more circular before chunkier shapes took over the game. That softer, more classic silhouette flatters square to angular face shapes especially well, and gives the Downing its staying power today. While heritage brands like Ray-Ban and Persol offer similar rounded styles, Warby Parker delivers a comparable timeless look and build at a much more accessible price.

The rounded lenses help soften sharper, more angular faces, but they’re not overly circular, which is why they still work on round and oval faces too. It’s one of those rare shapes that’s versatile across the board. I have a round face, and they look great with whatever vibe I’m going with. The keyhole bridge sits naturally on the nose (no adjustable pads), though it may not be a perfect fit for guys with lower or higher nose bridges. The acetate frame feels smooth yet durable, and the scratch-resistant lenses hold well if you drop them or toss them in your bag.

I also found that the temples are lightweight, so they don’t pinch behind your ears, making them easy to wear from the time I get to the office to the time I leave. The color—called English Oak—is like a toned-down tortoise that looks best with solid, everyday staples.

If you want a pair of sunglasses that you can throw on with anything, every day, The Napoli is the one. I’ve worn them with everything—think T-shirt and jeans, a polo and chinos, or even a hoodie and shorts. The square shape adds structure to rounder faces without looking too boxy on guys with sharper features. The keyhole bridge sits so comfortably on the nose, I don’t even feel it. I love the lens colors, which veer away from the super dark black lenses.

The gradient brown-to-yellow lenses are easy on the eyes in bright sun, giving a relaxed vibe. This also makes the sunnies more wearable—you can rock them in the bright sun or just walk around the city without feeling like you’re hiding behind your shades. The temples are slim but stay in place no matter how I move my head. While the acetate frame is lightweight and comfortable, it doesn’t offer the same durability as heavier acetate, so handle with care if you’re rough on glasses or tend to toss them in your bag.

Randolph began churning out military-spec aviators for the U.S. Air Force in the late 1970s, and its metal frames are still very stylish today. Unlike mass-produced sunglasses, each pair is handcrafted in the U.S., going through 200 steps over six weeks, which gives them a high-quality feel built to last a lifetime. I’ve had mine for three years now and wore them for the first time during a weekend getaway to Nantucket. I sported them on boat rides, walking along the pier, and during casual dinners. They performed flawlessly, reducing glare on the water and staying comfortable for hours. They’re perfect for everyday casual outfits like shorts, T-shirts, or polo shirts. They also pair nicely with slightly dressier looks, like linen button-downs or lightweight jackets.

The Skytech glass lenses are made from durable optical glass and deliver exceptional clarity, contrast, and anti-reflective performance, with both polarized and nonpolarized options available. The durable matte chrome frames with snug screws hold up well, while the clear bayonet-style temple tips slide gently along the side of your head instead of curving around your ears. They make the sunglasses easy to slip on and off and help them stay in place. This aviator shape works for most face types but is especially flattering on oval, square, and heart-shaped faces, balancing wider foreheads and softening softer jawlines. It’s not the best option for wider faces as it can make them appear even bigger.

Oakley’s Radar EV Path has those taller lenses perfect for athletes and anyone who spends a lot of time running, golfing, or cycling. This extended range of view really shows off the legendary Prizm lens, which makes colors pop and boosts contrast so you can see everything clearly. This wraparound design gives you extra coverage at the top, protecting your eyes from sunlight, wind, and debris. The no-slip nosepad and extended arms keep the glasses locked in place, even when you're sweating.

The lightweight, flexible frame plus adjustable nosepiece makes them comfortable for long sessions. Best for oval and medium-to-long faces, the wraparound style hugs the sides for a snug, secure fit. Small or very round faces can still wear them, but wider faces might find them a little tight. Heads-up: These are just made for performance and not style, so don’t try to sport them with a casual T-shirt or button-up at a dressy brunch.

Uniqlo delivers an affordable rectangular pair of sunglasses that don’t feel cheap. They look as sharp and polished as pairs that cost way more. The frames are made from flexible plastic that feel lightweight in hand but aren’t flimsy. Case in point: I dropped them more than once and even accidentally sat on them—fully expecting a snap. Somehow, the temples held strong and didn’t split in half. The thicker temples help here, too. The bridge and nose pads are molded into the frame, providing comfortable support. This pair of sunglasses lacks adjustable nose pads, so the fit may not work for those who have a low or high nose bridge.

The rectangular shape is especially great for rounder or softer face shapes, adding structure and making your features look sharper. If you’ve got a fuller face, this is one of the easiest ways to balance things out. Yes, these shades block sunlight effectively with enough coverage to keep glare out of your eyes without feeling oversized. I wore them on bright midday walks and didn’t find myself having to squint. If you’re looking for multiple color frames, Uniqlo doesn’t offer that with these shades. You can only get them in black, but that doesn’t limit your styling options.

Ray-Ban’s round sunglasses are a step up from your everyday pair, thanks to the gold metal rims and classic green lenses, which give off a more luxe, retro aesthetic. The thin metal build looks great and keeps the pair lightweight and sleek, but it’s more delicate than thicker frames.

The metal bridge with adjustable nose pads lets you fine-tune the fit, while the slim temples keep them comfortable. It’s perfect for vacation fits—easily pairing with swim trunks or an open camp shirt and linen shorts for a resort lunch. I’ve worn mine poolside in Costa Rica while lying in the sun, but they’ll also dress something like a tee and jeans if you don’t want to look too basic. It sits a bit closer to the face (petite fit), which makes it feel more styled than oversized. The round shape softens sharper features, but still works across the board for most guys. Bonus: These Ray-Ban’s come in a bunch of lens options—blue, brown, and gradients—so you can switch up the vibe.

Tortoise sunglasses are timeless, versatile, and universally flattering. This classy pair from Moscot looks good with lots of neutral items—think white tees, navy shirts, or olive chinos. You can also mix it with small or muted patterns like thin stripes, tiny checks, or small prints. These shades are made from real Italian acetate and come in a square-ish round silhouette that’ll always be in style. It’s offered in four sizes for a tailored fit. The keyhole nose bridge keeps them comfortable for more than six hours, and the rims feel robust without feeling overly heavy.

The rounded lenses work best on round and oval faces, thanks to its slight square edge that balances softer features. Caveat: Guys with very square or angular faces may find that the softer edges of this frame don’t add much definition, so the effect is more relaxed than structured. Also, I found these sunnies to be heavier than other picks that I’ve tested, which may feel bulky on smaller faces. They come in over 20 color options, but for an everyday classic look, the chestnut fade is a safe bet.

Persol's aviator shades offer a wider field of view and a serious level of coverage. These bold, square sunglasses are a great option for guys with round faces, but anyone can sport them.

In our testing, we found that the polarized, light blue lenses not only looked dope, but also offered scratch and shatter resistance to make sure these sunnies last a while. They look great worn for a lunch date with friends, but give real main character energy when you're tanning on the beach or poolside.

Another stylish but also functional standout is the 100 percent acetate frame, which we've found to be lightweight and sturdy. After using it for a full day at the beach, we hardly noticed that we were actually wearing it.

Rectangular sunglasses tend to look best on guys with rounded, oval, or heart-shaped faces. If that’s you, say hello to Oliver Peoples' version, which is a collaboration with tennis champ Roger Federer. Their sharper edges complement guys with softer facial features.

We found that these sunnies offer high-optical quality as well as style for days spent on and off the tennis court. Thanks to the adjustable rubber nose pads and temple tips, they rested gently on our face (even when we were playing) and felt more comfortable to wear all day long than any other rectangular frames we tested.

Look for frames that add structure—think square, rectangular, or angular aviators and wayfarers. These shapes balance softer features and make your face appear more defined.

Most frame shapes work, from round to square. Experiment with classic aviators, bold wayfarers, or even a round lens for a vintage vibe.

Opt for rounded or oval frames that soften a strong jawline. Circle lenses or softer rectangle shapes can help create balance.

Frames that are wider at the bottom or slightly curved help balance a broader forehead. Aviators, teardrop lenses, or rounded frames are good options.

High cheekbones and a narrow forehead and chin look great with rimless or oval frames of sunglasses because they emphasize your eyes and soften your facial angles.

When choosing a new pair of sunglasses, you should make sure that they provide 100 percent UV protection against both UVA and UVB rays. Otherwise, you can find yourself in a world of problems. "Excessive sun exposure could lead to cataracts and eye or eyelid cancer," Jeff Pettey, MD, clinical spokesperson for the American Academy of Ophthalmology, previously told MH. You don't have to spend a fortune on sunglasses, but it's a must that you find a pair that fits well. As for what type to consider, go with wraparound models as they block UV rays that come in from the side and shield against winds that can cause dry eyes.

Polarized lenses are designed to cut down harsh glare, which helps reduce eye strain and makes it easier to see clearly in bright conditions. That glare usually comes from light bouncing off flat surfaces like water, snow, or pavement, not just direct sunlight. Polarized technology works by filtering out light, so you’re not squinting or dealing with that blinding shine. Because of that, polarized sunglasses are especially useful for water sports and outdoor activities, while photochromic lenses (which adjust to changing light) are recommended for everyday use.

Finding the right pair of sunglasses has everything to do with a frame that works for your face, style, and how you live in them. Certain shapes can sharpen your features or balance them out, while the right style can pull together everything from a laid-back weekend fit to a more polished look. That’s why we focused on aviators, wayfarers, round, square, and sport frames—the same ones our team has tested across everyday wear, travel, and outdoor activities—so you’re getting options that look good and hold up in real situations.

To find the best sunglasses for men, our Men’s Health fashion team—led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan—has tested over 50 pairs since 2021. That means everything from daily commutes and office fits to tropical getaways, beach days, and long weekends on the water, along with more active use like running, hiking, and biking. We put each pair through the same hands-on process, evaluating style, comfort, fit, durability, and overall value.

We paid close attention to how they held up over time—whether the frames could handle sweat and movement, if the lenses reduced glare and eye strain, and whether they delivered reliable 100 percent UV protection. Just as important, we looked at versatility: Could one pair work across multiple settings, from casual everyday wear to more dressed-up occasions? We also compared them against top competitors in the category to make sure each pick truly stands out in its class. Read on for the best sunglasses for men from classic brands like Ray-Ban and Randolph to newcomers like Jimmy Fairly Paris to sporty ones like Oakley.

Acetate is a popular material for crafting frames since it combines both durability and style, allowing for a wide range of color and pattern options, and is thus frequently used in premium sunglasses. TR-90, a thermoplastic material, is known for its durability, flexibility, and resistance to impact, and thus can often be found in outdoorsy sunglasses. Nylon is lightweight and flexible while offering excellent durability, even being able to resist extreme temperatures. Other materials like stainless steel and titanium are simply no-brainers due to their outstanding durability and ability to withstand wear and tear over time.

Bitcoin (BTC), the world’s largest cryptocurrency, has recorded a multi-month high in daily trading volume as the cryptocurrency market remains in the grip of extreme volatility.

The massive spike in trading volume comes in the wake of one of the biggest sell-offs in BTC this year.

On Nov. 21, the world’s largest cryptocurrency dropped as low as around $55,100, a level last seen in September 2024. The sharp decline in Bitcoin prices came as risk assets tumbled amid rising concerns over the U.S. stock market and the artificial intelligence (AI) sector, which weighed on investor sentiment.

Following the sharp plunge, Bitcoin managed to make a stunning comeback as the flagship cryptocurrency recovered to trade back above $60,000 and briefly pushed toward the $61,000 mark.

The comeback, however, was short-lived as BTC lost ground again and tanked below the crucial $60,000 mark.

BTC is currently trading at around $58,879, rising 5.4% in the last 24 hours, as per the latest data from CoinGecko.

Furthermore, the world’s largest cryptocurrency has a 24-hour trading volume of around $43.8 billion and has regained a market cap of $1.18 trillion.

The new product lets users predict whether Bitcoin’s price will rise or fall over the next 30 seconds, with each trade starting its own prediction window. Featuring zero-slippage execution and rapid settlement, the product extends the familiar five- and fifteen-minute crypto prediction format to a shorter, individually timed experience. OmenX organizes the trading decision around a defined question: will an asset’s price be higher or lower at the end of a specified period? #5111. Bitcoin institutional holdings hit $29.78B – What changed in Q3?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Things have changed dramatically since the third quarter of 2026, when institutional interest in Bitcoin [BTC] increased. After three quarters of net selling, institutional investors resumed net purchases of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products (ETPs).

According to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period.  Notably, by the 30th of September, institutional investment managers held a record 356,491 BTC-equivalent, worth approximately $29.78 billion.

The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.

Together, they held 144,307 BTC-equivalent by the end of September, representing 40.5% of all Bitcoin ETP holdings reported by institutional managers. If looked back, their holdings have increased for nine consecutive quarters and are now 3.3 times higher than their March 2024 levels.

That being said, large banks played a major role in this accumulation, with Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley being among the biggest buyers during Q3.

Wells Fargo alone added 14,636 BTC-equivalent, taking its total holdings to 30,553 BTC-equivalent, making it the largest institutional holder of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs, overtaking Jane Street.

Institutional ownership also shifted, with hedge funds dropping from 50.6% in December 2024 to 19%, while financial advisors and wealth platforms increased their exposure. Of this, BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for 65.2% of institutional Bitcoin ETP holdings.

That said, Bitcoin ETP holdings fell by 38,531 BTC between the 30th of September and the 16th of November.

However, the tokenized ETP sector continued to struggle, with its market capitalization falling 6.2% to $595 million and trading volume declining to $160 million, as previously reported by AMBCrypto.

This comes as Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded net inflows of $2.65 billion in September 2026 and $3.52 billion in August, while July saw smaller inflows of $172.43 million. However, the trend reversed in October, with $515.03 million in net outflows, followed by significantly larger outflows of $3.47 billion in November 2026.

#5110. Anthony Scaramucci Predicts Bitcoin Bottom This Week

Bitcoin (BTC) bull and SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci has argued that the world's biggest cryptocurrency could find a critical bottom as soon as this week.

Scaramucci's comments follow the leading cryptocurrency's struggle to recover from a catastrophic crypto market crash that took BTC to its lowest price level in over two years.

In the latest episode of All Things Markets on Nov. 20, the SkyBridge Capital founder joined Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz to discuss a potential bottom for Bitcoin.

Scaramucci shared his view that Bitcoin could see its bottom on Nov. 25, citing the cryptocurrency's four-year halving cycle as the driving force behind his comments.

"Before we came on, I asked ChatGPT when's the expected halving for Bitcoin," Scaramucci explained.

"And then when are we 500 days out from that halving? And the estimate was November 25th," he added.

This prediction stems from the idea that Bitcoin's price trends could follow a predictable four-year cycle that coincides with the cryptocurrency's halving events, when the new BTC supply is cut in half.

This theory suggests that Bitcoin could find its major bottom around the 500-day mark before its next halving, expected in 2028.

However, these theories are by no means a certainty when it comes to predicting future price action, especially with the current level of institutional participation and macroeconomic forces impacting the crypto market to an unprecedented extent.

During the conversation, Novogratz also took note of Bitcoin's history of forming double bottoms during its four-year cycles.

"And every four years, Bitcoin double bottomed," Novogratz remarked.

At the time, the Galaxy Digital CEO's comments suggested a potentially positive scenario, as Bitcoin had been able to hold its psychological $60,000 price level.

"If it doesn't break 60, that could be a good sign," he noted.

Unfortunately for Bitcoin, the cryptocurrency subsequently crashed below this critical price point. This has left some wondering whether the cryptocurrency has already found its ultimate bottom.

During the same conversation, Novogratz suggested that Bitcoin's short-term outlook could largely depend on the current situation in the stock market.

Specifically, the billionaire said that a rebound in tech stocks could lead to a strong rally in Bitcoin's price.

"If we put in a bottom in the next couple days in the S&P here, down 3% from here, down 5% from here. And we have a rally back up. Man, Bitcoin is going to rally hard with it," Novogratz predicted.

However, he also warned that Bitcoin could see a lot of market-driven movements going forward, as opposed to crypto-specific movements.

"I think we're going to be stuck tethered to general sentiment and risk," he said.

Novogratz also believes that Bitcoin could trade in a range between $60,000 and $75,000 before a breakout or breakdown becomes apparent.

Bitcoin plunged to around $55,100 on Nov. 21, its lowest price level since September 2024, following another severe wave of sell-offs in the crypto market.

It then bounced back strongly to climb above $60,000 again, albeit briefly, before falling back to around $59,000 on Nov. 22.

#5109. Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300

Three separate market pressures just collided—pushing BTC to a level not seen since July.

Bitcoin plunged 4.35% over the past 24 hours, falling to $61,300 — its lowest level since early July — as a global sell-off in AI stocks, heavy withdrawals from Bitcoin ETFs and a wave of forced liquidations sent shockwaves through crypto markets.

By Friday morning, Bitcoin was struggling to stay above $61,500, putting it on track for its seventh consecutive weekly decline.

This drop wasn’t triggered by a single event. Instead, several pressures hit the market at once: growing concerns over AI valuations, institutional investors pulling money out of Bitcoin ETFs, and leveraged traders being forced to close their positions as prices fell.

The broader pullback was driven by a retreat from riskier assets as investors questioned lofty AI valuations.

On Thursday, November 19, AI company Anthropic made its highly anticipated debut on the Nasdaq. Shares opened at $111.50 against an IPO price of $83, briefly pushing the company’s valuation above $2 trillion. However, the successful IPO failed to lift sentiment across the technology sector.

As Anthropic began trading, Bitcoin fell from around $62,700 to $62,250 within roughly 30 minutes, while broader Nasdaq losses accelerated.

By the end of the session, the Nasdaq was down 2.3%, the S&P 500 had fallen 2%, and the Dow Jones lost 2.2%.

The sell-off spread to Asia, where South Korea’s KOSPI dropped approximately 5%, triggering a temporary restriction on automated selling.

Institutional demand for Bitcoin is also showing signs of weakening, adding further pressure to an already struggling market.

According to SoSoValue data, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.19 million in net outflows on November 19, marking the largest single-day withdrawal of the month.

With the exception of a modest $8 million inflow on November 5, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have faced nearly two weeks of persistent capital withdrawals, signaling a significant pullback in institutional demand.

As spot prices broke below key support levels, leveraged derivatives traders fueled a cascade of forced selling.

CoinGlass data shows $697.35 million in crypto positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours. About $600M came from long positions, and $201.25M of the total was Bitcoin longs.

According to market analyst Axel Adler Jr., Bitcoin remains under significant bearish pressure, with short-term investors sitting on substantial unrealized losses. Bitcoin is currently trading 15.7% below the average cost basis of recent buyers and has remained below that level for 12 consecutive days.

Until BTC reclaims the short-term holder cost basis and U.S. spot ETF flows flip back into positive territory, an analyst warns that the broader market correction isn’t over yet.

Bitcoin’s slide alongside AI stocks underscores how tightly crypto still tracks risk appetite in traditional markets. Continued ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations are likely to keep pressure on prices until broader market sentiment stabilizes.

#5107. Michael Saylor prioritizes STRC buybacks as Strategy’s Bitcoin buying slows 90% – Why?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Nothing highlights the impact of ongoing market volatility better than Strategy.

In a recent interview, Michael Saylor outlined a potential shift in Strategy’s approach. He explained why the company could sell MSTR shares even below its net Bitcoin value to buy back STRC. The key takeaway? The market is calling this arguably the most revealing part of the 19th of November’s investor Q&A.

Fundamentally, this seems logical. As outlined below, MSTR has performed extremely poorly as Bitcoin has fallen, losing over 40% of value within Q4. If MSTR loses another 25% of value, it will have lost more this quarter than last year’s Q4 crash, potentially making it the worst quarter MSTR has had since the bear market back in 2022.

The result? Strategy’s Bitcoin [BTC] accumulation has slowed sharply in Q4 2026.

In Q4 2025, Strategy bought 32,470 BTC. In comparison, it has only bought 3,183 BTC so far in Q4 2026. This represents a drop of 90%. To date, Strategy also used $206.3 million proceeds from selling MSTR shares to buy STRC shares. However, only $33.4 million has been used to buy Bitcoin.

In short, broader market weakness is putting Strategy under pressure. Against this backdrop, Michael Saylor’s latest STRC strategy doesn’t look like a random move. Strategy seems to be shifting more capital toward supporting its preferred stock while navigating a difficult market. But with FUD around the company continuing to build, the bigger question is whether STRC can still attract enough investor demand to support Strategy’s Bitcoin accumulation plans.

One thing is clear: Strategy’s main priority is to keep STRC stable.

As one analyst pointed out, this could mean the company would continue selling MSTR shares to fund STRC buybacks. If that isn’t enough, Strategy could also sell Bitcoin whenever STRC trades below its $100 par value. Saylor believes STRC’s 12% dividend is already attractive enough, making it a key income-generating product for institutional investors.

But what does this mean for Strategy shareholders? As the chart below shows, major institutional investors increased their MSTR holdings in Q3 2026. The top 15 now own around 33% of all outstanding shares. This shows that big investors are still interested in MSTR despite market weakness.

However, with Strategy focusing more on STRC, will MSTR shareholders still benefit from its BTC strategy?

Notably, this is where a potential feedback loop comes in. Continued weakness in MSTR could push Strategy to rely more on STRC buybacks to support its capital structure. However, this could also put institutional demand for MSTR at risk. If investor confidence weakens, raising fresh capital for future STRC buybacks could become more difficult.

So, for now, Saylor’s shift towards STRC signals a “risky” change in how Strategy plans to fund future BTC purchases.

Strategy is focusing more on STRC buybacks as MSTR struggles, potentially slowing Bitcoin purchases.

STRC’s 12% dividend may attract investors, but can it maintain demand without hurting MSTR?

But they're not only great for athletes or fitness buffs; a massage gun can help anyone relieve sore muscles, improve circulation, and mitigate stiffness after tough workouts.

I have a few members of my family who regularly steal my massage gun to address stiffness or aches while watching Netflix or between Zoom calls at their desk. "It won’t be the fix-all tool to dramatically improve your health, but it will be a valuable supplement to your routine," Sanchez adds.

But let's be real: The massage gun market has become totally saturated. And with so many options out there, it's hard to decipher which ones are actually worth your hard-earned cash. (Although if you really want to save some dough, you can attempt to turn a jigsaw into a massage gun.) While there are certainly some great budget massage guns, you have to be careful with what you choose.

With specific recovery routines and preferences in mind, our guide of massage guns represents some of the best options on the market right now—including a deep dive into our top-tested models from Theragun and Hyperice, the two most popular massage gun brands out there.

Discover why we love each percussion massage gun model below, then keep scrolling to read advice from our experts on what to look for and the best practices for use. Note that different companies refer to the speed as percussions per minute, shortened to PPMs, or revolutions per minute, shortened to RPMs. They mean the same thing, but for this story we use PPMs.

This is the massage gun that I keep at my desk both at home and at the office. That's because it offers noiseless performance and doesn't take up much space at all. The cost is less than most of its rivals in the space, and it packs as much of a punch as the full-sized models of both top brands.

This lightweight device weighs only 1.6 pounds, so it won't sit like a rock in your gym bag (or make your arms quake post-upper body lift). This also means you can easily grip and move it around your body without tiring out your arms. Hyperice markets this as a travel device, which it can be, but when it comes to taking up less room in your carry-on bag, the Theragun Mini (below) can't be beat.

The Hypervolt Go 3 is the update to the Hypervolt Go 2, which I was also a fan of. This update keeps what was great, and features small improvements, like a redesigned massage head that hits more surface area than the previous generations. This improvement goes across the new Hypervolt 3 line.

The device is fully charged when you take it out of the box, so all you need to do is hold down the power button to get rolling. It has three different percussion speeds and two different head attachments to vary your experience, so it's nearly as customizable as more premium models (you get two more percussion speed settings with the Hypervolt 3 Pro). Best of all, the motor on this machine is extremely quiet, which allows me to use it in scenarios where sound could be an issue.

As someone who leads a busy, on-the-go lifestyle and travels a lot, I've never utilized a massage gun as much as this compact one. Its scaled-down size and lightweight design make it practical to chuck in my carry-on, backpack, or gym/work bag, so I bring it out of the house with me nearly every day.

Despite its smaller size, this massage gun's performance stands out, delivering a powerful massage experience that's comparable to its larger counterparts. It weighs less than 1.5 pounds, has 150 minutes of battery life, three different speed settings, and three attachment heads, so you're not missing out on much that bigger models may offer. I will say, however, it does deliver a slightly more surface-level massage than the Theragun PRO (which I used before acquiring the Mini). That being said, the power and depth offered by the Mini is plenty for most people to reap the benefits of percussion therapy.

"This is hands-down my favorite massage gun. its small enough that I can travel with it anywhere, and despite its odd shape, I find it easy to hold and use," says Samuel. "It’s my go-to for loosening chest and IT bands."

For those interested in adding a few premium features, I've also tested the Theragun Mini Plus, which provides heat to the treatment area. And regardless of the need for heat application for better recovery in your case, it does provide a pleasant experience. I wouldn’t say it is necessary for the price, and this original design can’t be beat.

My only qualm with this thing is that it's noise level is a limiting factor in terms of where I actually use it. It's compact and lightweight enough to bring on-the-go, but it's definitely not quiet enough to use in a subdued office setting, for example. It's quieter than larger models, but not as dampened as you'd think for one so small.

This massage gun from Renpho is one of the most popular purchases on Amazon and we can see why. With four interchangeable massage heads and five speed settings, this sub-$100 device competes with the likes of Hyperice and Therabody for pennies on the dollar.

Featuring a minimalist, ergonomic design, this massage gun feels comfortable and manageable in my hand, targeting everything from my traps to calves. The motor is powerful, delivering a massage that falls somewhere between the Hypervolt 3 and the Theragun PRO in terms of intensity.

Its battery life also impressed me, but the charging itself took a little bit longer than other models on the market. Whether you're looking for an entry-level massage gun to test the waters or want to purchase a spare to leave at the office, this one is a no-brainer in terms of overall value.

For anyone looking for a suitably powerful and quiet full-sized model, this is the way to go. Sure, there is the standard Hypervolt 3, but for a little more money, you can get two additional power settings, which means more options when it comes to your treatment. And if you want something that packs slightly less of a punch and is more mobile, the Hypervolt 3 Go is a much better pick.

The max power level on this gun is less than others on the list, but I don't count that as a negative. Instead, the additional power settings allow you to access lower levels than other devices, which will be welcomed by many users like me.

For the variability and the performance that this massage gun delivers, the weight is very reasonable. The handle is easy to grip and gives you good stability when you want to dig into the muscles a little deeper.

Read More: Normatec Elite Compression Boots Review

The Theragun Prime Plus includes a 120-minute battery life, heated attachment, and a multi-grip handle that makes hard-to-reach areas more accessible. There are quite a few Theraguns on the market right now, and I've tested them all. Choosing between the many full-sized options can be difficult, but in my opinion, this is the standout amongst the crowd.

For the percussive force it distributes, the weight is surprisingly light. The unique design allows me to change up my grip however I wish. And unlike other premium options, it's light enough for you to actually handle it with each grip. The heated attachment provides comfort during your treatment, and while its warmth may not actually be scientifically proven to be effective in this application, it is pleasant during use.

Like the other higher-end Theragun models, the Prime Plus also has “smart” capabilities with the Therabody app, which allows users to track progress and data with Bluetooth connectivity. With four attachments, plus five different percussion settings with up to 60 pounds of force, this massager leaves nothing to be desired.

Ekrin has entered the world of massage gun devices and quickly made a noticeable splash. This powerful massager has a sleekly designed handle that looks basic but more than gets the job done. It's easy to use, and comes with six different massage heads to target muscle groups in different ways.

Our Health Director Marty Munson finds the ergonomic design impressive. "I have joint issues in my hands, but this grip is really comfortable," says Munson. "I've used many of the mainstay models out there, but I'm impressed with how good this one is."

The device also has six different speed settings and a rechargeable battery, which provides up to 8 hours of use on a single charge. It also delivers up to 3,500 percussions per minute, meaning it's a good option if power is toward the top of your massage gun must-haves list.

The Rally Orbital Massager stands out as a versatile and effective new tool in recovery, which is why it earned a spot in our Men’s Health Fitness Awards. Its ergonomic design fits comfortably in the hand, making it easy to maneuver across different muscle groups. The device offers multiple intensity levels, allowing you to customize the massage experience based on your specific needs, whether it’s for post-workout recovery or general tension relief.

Samuel is a fan, finding this device gentler than other options and perhaps more appropriate for a larger segment of the population. Even at higher intensities, the device operates with minimal noise, making it suitable for use in shared spaces or while watching TV. The battery life is also pretty solid.

Overall, the Rally Orbital Massager delivers excellent value for anyone seeking an accessible at-home massage solution, and manages to bring more innovation to a space that has been advancing for years. Its combination of thoughtful design, strong performance, and user-friendly features makes it a standout choice among other premium products.

To learn more about what to look for in a massage gun, we spoke with Vinh Pham, PT, a physical therapist and the founder of Myodetox, a manual therapy and movement clinic with locations in Canada and the U.S. According to Pham, the three most important things are reliability, noise, and battery life. "I need something that I know is well-made and won’t malfunction during operation, especially because I’m using it on injured athletes. Noise is the next most important factor. I need to be able to talk to my athletes over the noise of the gun without yelling at them."

Keeping treatment quiet is a major priority. "Personally, noise to me is number one," says Pham. "I want to be able to use the massage guns in public, and having it sound like a power tool would make it unusable." This is a feeling that I also agree with; especially when treating yourself around other people, you can feel self-conscious.

Next up is battery life, as PTs and athletes can’t have guns dying in the middle of treatment. Pham says that he expects a massage gun to last several full days without requiring a charge. "You’ll also want to be able to throw the gun in your bag or take it on a weekend trip without worrying about finding an outlet," Pham says.

Given the fact that massage guns are required to vibrate intensely in order to get the job done, it's not the kind of product you want to be sent with loose screws. Given how much the market has grown in recent years, there have been a lot of knockoff brands releasing subpar models that won't go the distance. Hands-on experience, like our team at Men's Health focuses on, is important in the research process. All of our picks have been vetted for durability, but it comes as no surprise that if you want the best and a brand name you can trust, you should expect to spend a little more.

Sufficient speed, or percussions per minute (PPM), plays a role in how the gun promotes blood flow. The higher the percussive rate, the more it can stimulate circulation. Look for a massage gun with a high percussive force and adjustable speed settings so you can deliver adequate force to different muscles. Another factor to consider is amplitude, which describes the amount of distance the massage head travels back and forth. This controls how effectively you can target certain muscle groups and how deeply the massager can get into the muscle tissue.

Just as important as amplitude is the gun's stall force, or the amount of pressure that the motor can apply to the muscle before it stops working. The higher the stall force, the more powerful a massage the gun can put out. Remember, though, that a massage gun shouldn't necessarily attack your muscles. In fact, for most people, less force is more. So don't get overly caught up in having the most "powerful" gun on the market; you likely won't need it to gain recovery benefits.

Different attachments can provide different massage techniques and sensations that may be suitable for different muscles. Many massage guns tout a host of attachments, but realize this: You'll likely just use a handful of these (or sometimes, your favorite one). So don't get deluded into purchasing because of multiple attachments. Once you've purchased your massage gun, be sure to properly research what attachments are effective for what muscles. Using the wrong attachment can dramatically alter the effectiveness of the massage gun.

A portable and lightweight massage gun is ideal, especially if you plan to use it on the go or travel with it. Consider the weight, size, and the case included.

Of course, even the best guns leave room for improvement. Some options come with convenient travel cases and charging stands—something Pham would like to see more products offer. He also mentions that dishwasher-safe attachment heads would make for easier cleaning. And, as the market continues to progress, he hopes for smaller (yet still powerful) designs and Bluetooth app integration.

As the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, part of my job is to evaluate the latest and greatest recovery gear available. I've used massage guns regularly for the past decade for muscle activation and post-training recovery. The testing pool for this list started with dozens of models across a range of price points, including the bestselling brands, both established and new. I tested each for several weeks, in multiple scenarios, including at home and at the gym.

In addition to my own testing, this guide was made with input and testing notes from other knowledgeable Men's Health editors, including MH Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S., and Senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM. We consulted with respected physical therapists like Vinh Pham, PT, at Myodetox and Renato Sanchez for expert advice. We evaluated each device for durability, effectiveness, ergonomics (for ease of use), and portability. We also considered price point, as many massage guns offer better overall value than others.

After all this testing and research, we found these massage guns that we recommend.

Sanchez recommends first asking yourself why you’re considering a massage gun. "What are you looking to get out of one? Is it for recovery, pain relief, or helping you reach your fitness goals? If you answered yes to any of those, then you might be a good candidate to add one to your shopping cart," he explains.

"Massage guns can be used as an alternative to the foam roller as a self-myofascial release tool," adds Pham. He notes that benefits include everything from decreased stress, pain, and tissue tension to enhanced recovery, blood circulation, and range of motion.

"You can use it pre-workout to warm up the muscles and post-workout to decrease tightness and soreness," says Pham.

You don’t want to spend hours upon hours using your massage gun. Instead, you’ll want to spend 90 to 120 seconds on any given muscle group, floating the gun across that area, according to Samuel. "Aim to follow the direction of the muscle fibers. That means running your gun across your chest, from the center toward your shoulder, instead of running it up and down your chest."

But be mindful to not run your massage gun across joints; you want to keep it focused on the soft tissue only. "And don’t try to aggressively drive the gun deep into the muscle, expecting more 'relief.' Using a massage gun shouldn’t hurt," explains Samuel.

Want to learn more on how you should be using one of these buzzy tools? Check out our how-to-use massage guns guide for instructions for best practices before, during, and after workouts.

Massage guns have gained a lot of popularity in recent years as a tool for muscle recovery—but do they really work? The blunt answer is they can. But it all depends on how, when, and where you use them.

These massagers offer rapid, percussive strokes designed to penetrate the muscle tissue, stimulate blood flow, and help break up adhesions. The research on the effectiveness of massage guns for muscle recovery is promising, but still limited.

A study published in the Journal of Clinical and Diagnostic Research found that using a massage gun on the quadriceps muscles after exercise resulted in a significant reduction in muscle soreness and an increase in muscle flexibility compared to a control group. Another study found that using a massage gun after exercise improved blood flow to the muscles and reduced muscle fatigue.

So, they can help with muscle soreness with correct use, but shouldn't be used as a replacement for other recovery methods such as rest, proper nutrition, active stretching, and dynamic mobility work.

We asked Sanchez how folks can get to those hard-to-reach areas with their massage guns. Here's his take: "Massage guns mainly target superficial muscles making it hard to isolate deeper musculature. Therefore, yes, the location of muscles can impact the effectiveness of this modality.

I think it’s safe to say the majority of people can reach the front side of their bodies using a massage gun, but you’ll need decent shoulder mobility if you’re looking to target the mid and low back. That’s when you’d want to get a massage gun that is more ergonomic or can be adjusted.

If mobility is a limiting factor, you may consider trading the massage gun for a lacrosse ball for pinpoint contact. Sometimes you might just be better off asking a friend, what’s the saying … I’ll scratch your back if you scratch mine?"

Charles Thorp is the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, where he shares the best product recommendations in gym equipment, recovery tools, supplements, and more. Following an early life in athletics, Charles became a NASM-certified trainer and began writing programs alongside the most respected coaches in the world.   Since entering the world of fitness content, Charles has had the opportunity to learn from and train alongside high performance individuals from the NFL, UFC, NBA, Formula 1, CrossFit, US Olympics, and Navy SEALs. When he’s not writing about training programs or gear, he can be seen at the gym or in the wild, putting them to the test.

He's logged training time with NFL athletes and track athletes and his current training regimen includes weight training, HIIT conditioning, and yoga. Before joining Men's Health, he served as a sports columnist and tech columnist for the New York Daily News.

#5104. GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia

Tokenized Take-Two shares saw a massive 24-hour trading spike as on-chain markets attract Washington scrutiny.

The long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI didn’t just break gaming records—it briefly turned publisher Take-Two Interactive into the hottest stock on the blockchain, outselling even AI giant Nvidia.

On November 18, decentralized exchange (DEX) trading volume for tokenized Take-Two shares (TTWO) exploded by 578%, jumping from $36.8 million to $249.5 million in a single day, according to Token Terminal data.

That was roughly 2.8 times the $88.1 million traded in tokenized Nvidia (NVDA) shares over the same 24-hour window, accounting for 42% of all on-chain stock trading.

Nearly all of the action, roughly $239 million, or 96% of total volume, happened on Solana via Backpack Securities, a subsidiary of crypto exchange Backpack. Launched earlier this year, the token is designed to be backed 1:1 by real Take-Two shares held in custody.

Traditional Wall Street traders saw a much calmer reaction: Take-Two’s Nasdaq shares rose 6.2% to close at $216.61 on launch day before pulling back 3.7% to $208.65 the next session.

Despite Take-Two’s one-day viral spike, Nvidia remains the undisputed heavyweight of tokenized equities, boasting a $399.4 million market cap and $2 billion in 30-day trading volume (compared to Take-Two’s $808.1 million).

Overall, tokenized public stocks on Solana have nearly doubled since late October to reach $1.22 billion.

That rapid growth is drawing fresh scrutiny in Washington. On November 16, four Democratic senators sent a letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) questioning how its newly introduced exemption for tokenized securities would address investor protection and anti-money laundering requirements.

The issue also surfaced during the November 19 Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing for Kristin Johnson, President Donald Trump’s nominee for the SEC. Johnson indicated that exemptions covering tokenized stocks should eventually be formalized through rules following a public comment period.

The TTWO spike shows tokenized stocks can attract event-driven trading on-chain, comparable to some of the largest names in the segment. It also coincides with growing regulatory scrutiny of how tokenized stocks are supervised.

#5102. VanEck ends Gemini deal for 3 crypto ETFs – What’s next for VSOL?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

VanEck has terminated Gemini as custodian and clearing agent for three U.S. crypto ETFs. In doing so, it has made Coinbase Custody its sole remaining safekeeper, thus putting into jeopardy the Solana fund’s staking future.

As per three 8-K filings from the 19th of November, VanEck Digital Assets delivered written termination notices to Gemini Trust Company on the 16th of November, with the contract set to officially end on 16th February.

The notice ended custody and clearing arrangements for the VanEck Bitcoin ETF (HODL) and the VanEck Ethereum ETF (ETHV).

The third ETF, the VanEck Solana ETF (VSOL), is the most affected one in this regard, because there is no news on who will take over staking services for it. Market participants are assuming it is Coinbase, but as of now, there is no confirmation yet.

As expected, the filings have opened a series of questions, as they have not established the allocation of assets between Gemini and Coinbase. This, in turn, has made it impossible to quantify precisely what Gemini is losing in dollar terms.

The filing also failed to explain why VanEck chose to terminate the agreements now, with roughly three months of notice before the effective date. Moreover, they did not even address the staking question that matters most for VSOL shareholders.

This comes as the crypto ETF landscape has been in a consolidation for a while now, with Coinbase already being a custodian for most U.S. Spot crypto ETFs.

All in all, VanEck’s current decision to put an end to its Gemini arrangements has left it with a single custodian across all three funds and a massive unresolved operational gap.

What’s left now is that by 16th February, 2027, the firm will have to find a new staking provider for VSOL.

#5099. Ethereum Drafts New Gas Rules for Validator Deposits

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ethereum developers want to change the gas accounting for validator deposits. The plan is to measure the request bytes that these deposit events create.

The gas calculation already accounts for executing a deposit. However, after the deposit is finished, a 192-byte request is passed along with the block. Those 192 bytes are excluded from the minimum gas charge, so the same gas limit might allow more data than the initial calculation accounts for.

Under Gloas, there is no fixed cap on the number of deposit requests per block. The execution layer has not capped this either. Gas is the only limiting factor.

Neither EIP-8131 nor EIP-8279 accounts for those request bytes. This means that deposits could become another way to bypass the gas floor once EIP-8279 closes the loophole involving cold storage reads.

A relay contract can call the deposit contract repeatedly, costing around 26,000 gas per deposit. In the author's example, that execution cost is below the point where the gas floor for zero-byte calldata would start to increase the total charge.

This results in a payload of about 1.44 times the block gas limit divided by 64, compared with about 1.15 times the same baseline.

The main issue is the data size, so the proposal directly addresses the data.

A log from the deposit contract with the deposit event topic counts as 192 bytes before the log entry is added. This is the same condition EIP-6110 uses to turn logs into requests.

The cost of this would be another check that client developers would have to implement and test.

Users are not expected to pay more for regular deposits. The cost of executing a regular deposit is already above the proposed minimum, so the extra 12,288 gas only raises the minimum charge.

The proposal has yet to be scheduled for a network upgrade.

#5098. Bitcoin’s price hits ‘bottom territory’ after BTC falls below $60K — What next?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Less than half of all Bitcoin [BTC] is green right now, and that’s not a good look. In fact, as it turns out, we may not see light anytime soon.

As of 18th November, those are the numbers. At least according to the Rand Group.

Every major BTC bottom since 2015 has happened with less than half the supply in the green. In August 2025, that figure was 35.7%. It hit 39.8% in December 2018, 42.5% in March 2020, and 44.8% in November 2022.

Each low has come in a little higher than the one before. Holders are giving up less ground with every cycle. The argument is that the best opportunities show up when most holders are underwater, not when everyone’s celebrating.

Hence, the question: Does that mean the bottom is in? No, But Bitcoin is in a zone where that has mattered before.

… might be tech stocks and rates, according to QCP Capital.

Not everyone’s ready to call it a bottom, yet. In fact, the digital asset partner thinks Bitcoin’s problem is about money getting tight everywhere.

Earlier this cycle, ETF buying, corporate treasuries, and hopes of rate cuts did a good job of soaking up selling. That support will crack when stocks drop across the board.

So, what would it take to turn things around?

…recovery will likely require stabilisation in technology equities, reduced volatility in rates and evidence that institutional flows are returning.

Until then, any bounce driven by shorts closing out could fizzle fast. The Fed could also be another weight on BTC’s back.

At the time of writing, the charts weren’t really comforting either. BTC was trading at $58,681, down 5.2% over the last 24 hours. Just a couple of weeks ago, it was trading above $80K.

The RSI was knee deep in oversold territory, its lowest reading in months. Sellers have been running out fuel, but oversold conditions can stay as such for a while.

The ADX was 43.8 and still rising. So, the downtrend seemed to be getting stronger. Especially since buyers didn’t look like they were going to turn up.

This is a bottom range that we know. However, until the selling pressure slows down, calling it the floor would be a gamble.
